FILE: research/audits/api_inputs/2026-11-12-accelerated/character-build.md
Constructive algorithm obligation: remove the factorial split-mask cost for uniform growing-degree native Legendre reconstruction. Input odd p, degree d, coherent chosen BIT oracle for padded F(x)=chi(Q(x)), chi(0)=+1, unknown monic squarefree Q degree d. Target recover Q in poly(d,logp,log1/eta), under an explicit polynomial threshold p>=poly(d). Existing result in supplied notes costs exp(O(d logd)); the exact same split Hankel receiver cannot have polynomial success even for irreducible Q. Candidate different operation: prepare a broad (not only completely split) coefficient state with phase chi(Res(Q,R)), or another explicit collective operation yielding polynomial-probability recoverable moments. Derive this from BASE-FIELD character queries; no extension-field Q oracle, value queries, roots, free preparation inverse or secret quotient algebra. Try the cheapest classical/black-box attacks before proposing quantum gates. Native coefficient interpolation uses full values and is not available. A concrete end-to-end route or a proved decisive falsifier of this new phase-synthesis mechanism is useful. Merely improving the closed split-receiver analysis is not.

# One-sample Hankel readout for native character reconstruction

2026-11-05. Independently reviewed written uniform parameterized algorithm.
It runs in exp(O(d log d)) times a polynomial in the
remaining input parameters. It is NOT polynomial in d, a novelty claim,
a classical separation, or an executed quantum algorithm.

## Scientific contract and the new operation

Let p be an odd prime and Q in F_p[X] an unknown monic squarefree polynomial
of degree d>=2. Unlike the earlier fixed-degree statements, d is an input
parameter here. The source supplies fresh pure tensor copies

    |phi_F>=p^(-1/2) sum_x F(x)|x>,  F:F_p->{+1,-1}.

In the clean case F=lambda composed with Q, where lambda(0)=+1 and
lambda(z)=chi_p(z) otherwise. In the robust case ONE FIXED F disagrees
with this padded table at at most rho*p positions, for public
0<=rho<1/4 and kappa=1-4rho. A coherent BIT oracle or uncontrolled padded
raw phase unitary supplies one copy per query. No extension-field oracle,
unknown preparation inverse, root flags or hidden factorization is given.
Mixed/device noise, varying masks and correlated banks are outside the model.

The new operation uses m=2d-1 native copies and encodes a public split
polynomial R of degree m. A Fourier outcome has 2d coordinates. On the
support of a VIRTUAL comparison state, these are trace moments of Q's
quotient algebra. ONE such outcome determines Q by an invertible d-by-d
Hankel system. This replaces the previous requirement for d independent
good hyperplane samples. It also removes the subtraction of proper-subspace
mass from the success proof: the entire virtual support is decodable.

The clean all-flags success bound per attempt is 1/(32m!). With fixed
corruptions it is 1/(32*36^m*m!). Public postprocessing, source conversion,
factor erasure and Fourier gates have polynomial cost in d and log p.
The resulting total cost is exp(O(d log d)), with only a polynomial prime
threshold. This removes the older exp(O(d^2 log d)) block-retry dependence
and factorial prime threshold; it does not remove the split-mask factorial.

The external problem is the published native character reconstruction
query/time gap. Corpus been-tried found related Prony/recurrence primitives
but no exact native composition; a textual search is not a novelty result.
Prony/Hankel reconstruction from 2d supplied moments is known. See
audits/sources/legendre_prf/kaltofen_prony_2022.txt, opening discussion,
and the existing Cayley--Hamilton/Hankel recurrence bridge in the repository.
The work here pays those moments from ORIGINAL character-only copies and
proves their source probability. Childs et al., arXiv:1509.09271, Theorem 3,
uses full FIELD-VALUE polynomial queries; that oracle is not available here.
Its fixed-degree efficient interpolation result cannot be imported as a
character-query decoder. Russell--Shparlinski supplies an O(d)-query POVM,
not this circuit. No primitive or overall priority claim is made.

## 1. Paid degree-m split coefficient source

Take m copies of phi_F and project onto distinct x_1,...,x_m. This succeeds
with alpha=(p)_m/p^m, since every F(x) is a sign. Reversibly sort and retain
the permutation rank. The symmetric phase product makes that rank an
independent uniform state on m! labels; unprepare it without postselection.
Append a coherent uniform a in F_p^* with the PUBLIC phase

    chi_p(a)^d,

where d is the TARGET degree, not the number m of roots. Form the coefficient
vector of R=a product_i(X-x_i), in ascending order. Erase the canonical
roots using the paid public factorization inverse described below. The
resulting normalized state is supported on all squarefree completely split
degree-m R, a set of size N_m=(p-1)binom(p,m), with phase

    chi_p(a)^d product_i F(x_i).

The target-degree exponent is essential. The resultant identity is

    Res(Q,R)=(-1)^(dm) a^d product_i Q(x_i).

Because m=2d-1 is odd, the global sign is chi_p(-1)^d. Blindly calling an
m-copy helper that uses chi_p(a)^m gives the wrong source for even d.
It cannot be repaired by renaming an exponent in the probability analysis.

All source-conversion operations are uniform in m. Compute m!, rank and
unrank permutations using their Lehmer codes in poly(m) integer operations
on O(m log m) bits. Prepare the uniform rank state on [0,m!-1] with binary
prefix-count rotations, not a hardcoded circuit or an enumerated m! table.
This realizes the exact ideal tensor-factor removal with polynomial-size
approximation circuits. Polynomial multiplication maps roots to coefficients
in polynomially many field operations.

For clean root erasure use the previous public-shift procedure: L independent
uniform shifts, L=ceil(log2(8p^2/eta)), distinguish every pair of field
elements by their Legendre trit signatures with failure<=eta/16. Gcds with
X+t_j and (X+t_j)^((p-1)/2) +/-1, taken modulo the current public factors,
split EVERY supported degree-m R into linear factors on that one good-seed
event. The number and sizes of operations are polynomial in m,log p,L.
Canonical sorting then permits reversible root erasure. The factorization
is of PUBLIC R, never hidden Q. Bounded uniform shift sampling retains the
previous <=eta/8 ABORT budget. No domain-sized signature table is stored.

## 2. Virtual quotient-algebra Fourier law

For the proof only, let A=F_p[X]/Q, theta=X mod Q. Squarefreeness makes
A a product of fields F_(p^d_j). Put U=product_j(p^d_j-1). The linear map

    L_Q: V_m=F_p^(m+1) -> A,  coeff(R) |-> R(theta)

is surjective, with kernel Q times all polynomials of degree<=m-d.
The kernel has dimension m+1-d. The virtual normalized state is

    |N_Q>=[p^(m+1-d)U]^(-1/2)
           sum_R chi_p(Res(Q,R)) |coeff(R)>.

It is never prepared. Its norm character is the product of the nontrivial
quadratic characters on the field components and vanishes on nonunits.
The additive Fourier transform of N_Q is supported on H=(ker L_Q)^perp.
With the nondegenerate trace pairing, every frequency there has a unique
description

    y_j=Tr_(A/Fp)(t theta^j),  0<=j<=m,  t in A.

Either Fourier sign convention gives the same set (replace t by -t).
Exactly the unit t contribute: all field components of t must be nonzero.
The component Gauss sums and kernel normalization give magnitude 1/sqrt(U)
on these U frequencies and zero elsewhere. This proves a Fourier law;
it does not supply A, theta, t, Q's factors or an extension oracle.

## 3. Every virtual supported outcome determines Q

Given a measured y=(y_0,...,y_(2d-1)), form

    H_y=(y_(i+j))_(0<=i,j<d),
    v_y=(y_d,...,y_(2d-1))^T.

If H_y is singular, abort this attempt. Otherwise solve q=-H_y^(-1)v_y
and construct C=X^d+sum_(j=0)^(d-1) q_j X^j. Keep it only if squarefree.
This is polynomial-time finite-field linear algebra and a public gcd check.

For a virtual supported frequency, H_y is the Gram matrix in the basis
1,theta,...,theta^(d-1) of

    B_t(a,b)=Tr_(A/Fp)(tab).

The trace pairing of an etale algebra is nondegenerate. Multiplication by
the unit t is invertible, so B_t and H_y are nondegenerate. Moreover
Tr(t theta^i Q(theta))=0 for i=0,...,d-1, giving exactly
H_y*(Q_0,...,Q_(d-1))^T=-v_y. Hence the public decoder returns Q on EVERY
virtual supported label, including arbitrary squarefree factor patterns.
Nonunit t can give singular Hankel matrices; they have zero virtual mass.
The proof needs the unit/cyclicity condition, not merely Cayley--Hamilton.

Let D_Q be the set of measured labels whose Hankel decoder actually returns
Q. It is an analysis event, not an available target-dependent predicate.
The support of F N_Q is contained in D_Q. Thus for the actual encoded state S,

    Pr_(F S)[D_Q] >= |<F N_Q,F S>|^2 = |<N_Q,S>|^2.

This bounds CORRECT decoding, not the probability that a random Hankel
matrix is nonsingular. Nonsingular outcomes returning a wrong polynomial
are handled by verification. No inlier recognizer is supplied.

## 4. Clean success and polynomial field threshold

Let r<=d be the number of rational Q roots. Exactly
N_good=(p-1)binom(p-r,m) supported R are coprime to Q. On those R the
clean source phase and virtual phase agree up to the single global sign;
on other R the virtual amplitude is zero. The exact squared overlap is

    gamma_clean^2=N_good^2/[N_m p^(m+1-d) U].

For p>=256d^2, alpha>=1/2, and N_good/N_m>=1/2: a uniform distinct
m-tuple hits a root of Q with probability at most mr/p. Also U<=p^d and
N_m/p^(m+1)=(1-1/p)alpha/m!>=1/(4m!). Therefore

    gamma_clean^2>=1/(16m!),
    Pr[distinctness flag AND decode Q]>=1/(32m!).

The true prime threshold is polynomial in d. There is no proper-subspace
escape subtraction requiring p to exceed a factorial. The factorial remains
in the split-source density and therefore the number of repetitions.

## 5. Fixed corruptions: a uniform signed-moment bound

For the same one fixed corrupted F as in the robust contract, let n=p-r
and B be the number of corrupted nonroot positions. The overlap magnitude is
gamma_clean times the absolute value of

    E_m = sum_j (-1)^j binom(B,j)binom(n-B,m-j) / binom(n,m).

Errors at Q roots do not contribute to this overlap. They are retained in
the actual source and are covered separately in verification. Put S=n-2B.
The generating polynomial (1+z)^(n-B)(1-z)^B shows that normalized signed
subset moments E_k satisfy

    E_0=1, E_1=S/n,
    (n-k)E_(k+1)=S E_k-k E_(k-1).

At p>=4d and rho<=1/4, S/n>=1/3. If n>=36m, inductively every ratio
R_k=E_k/E_(k-1) is positive and >=1/6: the base ratio is >=1/3, and

    R_(k+1)=(S-k/R_k)/(n-k)
           >=(n/3-6k)/(n-k)>=1/6   for k<=n/36.

Consequently E_m>=6^(-m). This direct recurrence is stronger than using
an absolute IID-coupling error; it needs only polynomial n in m. The
condition p>=256d^2 implies n>=p-d>=36m for every d>=2. We obtain

    Pr[distinctness flag AND decode Q]>=1/(32*36^m*m!).

The small-field Krawtchouk cancellation examples remain valid outside these
conditions. No independence of error positions or averaging over masks is
assumed. This is uniform over EVERY fixed F within the promised radius.

## 6. Verification, total resources and active memory

Use the statistical public-candidate verifier already proved in
LEGENDRE_CORRUPTED_CHARACTER_READOUT.md. With kappa=1-4rho,

    p>=max{256d^2,64d^2/kappa^2}

ensures true candidate acceptance probability at least beta^2,
beta=1-2rho, and wrong candidate acceptance at most 1/4. The latter follows
from the shared-factor Weil correlation bound plus 2rho changes. Set
Delta=beta^2-1/4 and tau=(beta^2+1/4)/2. For clean input one may take
rho=0 and the cleaner generation bound.

Set q0=1/(32m!) in the clean case, or 1/(32*36^m*m!) in the robust case.
Allocate total generation-circuit operator error<=q0/8 per attempt, so
the true candidate probability remains >=q0/2. Choose

    R=ceil((2/q0)ln(4/eta)),
    K=ceil((8/Delta^2)ln(8R/eta)).

At most R attempts are made. Each verification uses K NEW source copies;
accept when its empirical projection mean is >=tau. Per-test event error
<=Delta/8 and threshold rounding error<=Delta/8 retain the Hoeffding margin.
Missing all true candidates costs <=eta/4; all classification errors cost
<=eta/8; public seed failure and capped samplers cost <=eta/16 and eta/8.
The total is <=9eta/16. Approximate gates are already included in these
event bounds, not counted twice. Copies are capped by R(m+K), not R(d^2+K).
The verifier uses the inverse preparation of PUBLIC candidate states only.

Reversible permutation ranking, uniform interval states, polynomial
arithmetic, public root erasure, the m+1 arbitrary-modulus QFTs and the
Hankel solve have gate-generation and execution cost polynomial in
d,log p,log(1/eta),log(kappa^(-1)) and the requested precision. Kitaev's
paid approximate QFT and all input-padding rules are unchanged. Generation
precision has log(q0^(-1))=O(d log d); it does not create exponential
precision bit lengths. Verification has polynomial kappa^(-1) sample cost.
Consequently total gates and copies are

    exp(O(d log d))*poly(log p,kappa^(-1),log(1/eta)).

ACTIVE quantum and classical workspace is polynomial in these bit/degree
parameters. Request only the m copies for the current attempt; after the
Fourier measurement keep its classical candidate and request verification
copies sequentially. Do not retain R attempts or a bank of all future copies.
Public seeds occupy O(L log p) bits; permutation ranks occupy O(m log m);
root/polynomial workspaces and reversible histories are polynomial; retry
counters need O(log R) bits. No table of p values, m! permutations or all
candidate polynomials is stored. The large resource is TIME/repetitions.

## Classical comparison, falsifiers and current status

The native F problem and classical access have not changed. Kopparty's
full-table poly(p) decoder applies below its proved approximately 1/8
radius and degree condition; it is not extended here to 1/4. Throughout
rho<1/4, classical empirical exhaustive decoding uses poly(d,log p,
kappa^(-1),log(1/eta)) BIT queries and p^d candidate enumeration. Earlier
quasilinear cubic and sqrt(p) quadratic attacks retain their exact promises.
These are upper bounds, not hardness. No classical value queries are
silently supplied in the phase-copy-only model. The baseline campaigns
were reused because the native input/target is unchanged.

Required falsifiers: the scalar exponent must use TARGET d; every virtual
unit label must give invertible Hankel and the correct Q; nonunit/cyclic
failure must not be ignored; actual success must count D_Q, not all
nonsingular outcomes; the m! density and every source flag must remain
charged. The prespecified finite control checks these on five small clean
and corrupted cases. It does not simulate coherent source preparation or
the full quantum circuit and cannot prove the asymptotic theorem.

Independent review accepted the actual complete note and resource ledger:
[review](audits/reviews/2026-11-05-hankel-resultant-review.md).
The [control](classical_baselines/hankel_resultant_control.py) and
[artifact](classical_baselines/hankel_resultant_control.json) cover exactly
four clean sources and one fixed corrupted source. Their virtual support
sizes are 16,24,288,342; every supported label has full Hankel rank and
returns Q, while every virtual zero inside the annihilator is singular.
Actual Q-decoding mass exceeds the exact squared-overlap bound in each case.
Both quadratic cases have zero comparison overlap if the old chi(a)^m
phase is left uncorrected; omitting the correction chi(a)^(d-m), not
literally omitting chi(a)^d (which is 1 for even d), is the negative control.
The p7 mixed-cubic single-flip source has exact E5=-2/3.

All five finite sources have some wrong candidate with public projection
score 1. The corrupted cubic table is exactly another polynomial's padded
table, so its true Q is not even a nearest-table candidate. Every tested
prime is below the theorem threshold. These are algebra/overlap controls
and explicit small-prime identifiability failures, not demonstrations of
the complete verifier or asymptotic success. Exact field/rank/solve algebra
and floating FFT were used; no coherent circuit was run.

Primary sources used for the known-primitive and access-model checks are
[Kaltofen, Sparse Polynomial Hermite Interpolation (2022)](https://users.cs.duke.edu/~elk27/bibliography/22/Ka22herm.pdf)
and [Childs et al., Optimal quantum algorithm for polynomial interpolation](https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.09271).
Their local texts are kaltofen_prony_2022.txt and
optimal_interpolation_1509_09271.txt under audits/sources/legendre_prf/.
Kopparty's [noisy polynomial reconstruction paper](https://www.math.toronto.edu/swastik/weil-decoding.pdf)
records the native character query/time distinction; its proved algorithm
and degree constants remain as audited in the classical reduction review.

The operation is admitted after corpus/primary checks, with no novelty
conclusion. The next uniform-polynomial question remains how to remove the

# Actual success boundary of the split-source Hankel receiver

2026-11-05. Closed mathematical question: a sharper analysis of the SAME
2d-1-root coefficient Fourier/Hankel operation cannot give inverse-polynomial
success in growing d. An elementary packing argument proves this already
for every clean irreducible target. No arithmetic-progression splitting
hypothesis, finite scan, general quantum lower bound, novelty, or classical
hardness claim is used.

Read the current `STATE.md` and `TRAPS.md` before this derivation. The
operation is the one specified in `LEGENDRE_HANKEL_RESULTANT_READOUT.md`.
The question was whether its actual Q-specific success could be much larger
than the virtual-overlap factorial lower bound. It can exceed that lower
bound, but cannot become inverse polynomial in d.

## Exact residue-fiber law

Let Q in F_p[X] be monic irreducible of degree d>=2, let m=2d-1, and assume
p>=m so the distinct-root source exists. Let S be the set of squarefree,
completely split polynomials of exact degree m with nonzero leading
coefficient. Write

    N=|S|=(p-1)binom(p,m),
    A=F_p[X]/(Q),
    L:F_p[X]_{<=m}->A,
    K=|ker L|=p^(m+1-d)=p^d,
    C_v=#{R in S:R mod Q=v}.

Here K is a cardinality, not a verification repetition count. Since Q is
irreducible of degree at least two, no R in S is divisible by Q, so C_0=0.
For the normalized CLEAN coefficient state, all amplitudes within a residue
fiber have the same phase: up to the known global resultant sign it is

    psi_R=chi_A(v)/sqrt(N),  v=R mod Q.

Let H=(ker L)^perp in coefficient Fourier space. Projection onto H is
averaging over the K-element residue fibers in the original coefficient
basis. Consequently the exact conditional Fourier probability is

    Pr(H)=sum_v C_v^2/(N K).                                      (1)

For irreducible Q, the Q-specific correct Hankel-decoder event is EXACTLY
D_Q=H\{0}, not merely a superset containing the virtual support. To check
the converse direction, the first d entries of any y determine a unique
t in A by nondegeneracy of the trace pairing. If the Hankel solve returns
Q, its d equations impose the recurrence of Q on y_d,...,y_(2d-1).
Induction therefore forces every entry to equal Tr(t theta^j). Invertible
Hankel then means t!=0. The forward direction is the reviewed trace-Gram
argument. Hence

    Pr(D_Q)=sum_v C_v^2/(N K)
       - |sum_v chi_A(v)C_v|^2/(N p^(m+1)).                      (2)

The second term is the actual zero-frequency probability, which must not be
counted as a decodable outcome. For odd d it vanishes by scalar symmetry:
C_(av)=C_v for a in F_p^*, while chi_A(a)=chi_p(a)^d and sum_a chi_p(a)=0.
For even d no such automatic cancellation is asserted.

Equations (1)--(2) concern the state CONDITIONED on the known distinctness
projection. The joint ideal per-attempt correctness multiplies (2) by
alpha=(p)_m/p^m. All failed source attempts consume their original copies.

## An elementary packing upper bound

Fix a residue v. Suppose distinct R,R' in its fiber share d rational roots
x_1,...,x_d. Then Q divides R-R', and product_i(X-x_i) also divides R-R'.
These two divisors are coprime because Q is irreducible of degree>=2.
Their product has degree 2d, whereas deg(R-R')<=m=2d-1. Thus R-R'=0,
a contradiction. This also excludes distinct leading scalars on one root
set within a fiber; coefficients, not merely monic root sets, are counted.

Each R contributes binom(m,d) d-element subsets of its roots. No such subset
is contributed by two distinct R in the same residue fiber. There are only
binom(p,d) available subsets, so for EVERY v,

    C_v binom(m,d)<=binom(p,d).

Using sum_v C_v=N in (1) gives

    Pr(D_Q)<=Pr(H)<=max_v C_v/K
      <= binom(p,d)/(p^d binom(2d-1,d))
      <= (d-1)!/(2d-1)!
      = 1/[d(d+1)...(2d-1)]
      <= d^(-d).                                                 (3)

This is an exact all-p bound under the stated source support conditions.
The joint all-flags probability is no larger. For p>=256d^2, combine it
with the reviewed clean lower bound 1/(32(2d-1)!): the ideal clean
irreducible-target success has exp(-Theta(d log d)) order, uniformly in
that regime. Improving constants or the probability analysis cannot turn
this operation into an inverse-polynomial-success receiver.

## Reweighting or rephasing this support cannot fix it

There is a useful stronger scope statement that still concerns only THIS
coefficient support and Fourier/Hankel measurement. For ANY normalized
coefficient state psi supported on S, Cauchy-Schwarz in each fiber gives

    Pr_psi(H)=(1/K)sum_v |sum_(R in S:L(R)=v) psi_R|^2
       <=(1/K)sum_v C_v sum_(R in S:L(R)=v)|psi_R|^2
       <=max_v C_v/K.

Thus (3) also applies to arbitrary phases and weights on the same split
support, including fixed corrupted F sources. The exact C_v^2 identity (1)
is specific to the uniform clean source; the upper bound is not. The same
inequality extends to mixed states or retained ancillary workspace by
convexity/vector-valued Cauchy-Schwarz, provided the measured coefficient
register remains supported on S and the successful event is the same D_Q.

This rules out obtaining polynomial-degree success merely by refining the
overlap estimate, altering split-source weights, or changing its phases.
It does NOT rule out a different coefficient support, a different collective
measurement, use of information from multiple outcomes in another decoder,
or other quantum circuits. It is not a general query/copy/time lower bound.
The reviewed exp(O(d log d)) algorithm remains valid. Its exponentially
small per-attempt success is an actual feature of this operation, not only
an artifact of its overlap lower bound. A new end-to-end improvement must
change something outside the above support/measurement contract.

## Overcomplete packets and consecutive-window decoding

6 November 2026. Independent core derivation and actual-text mathematical
review accepted. This pass tests a CONCRETE attempted repair: use m>=2d-1 native
copies (for example m=O(d logd)), keep the resulting degree-m split
coefficient register, Fourier transform it, and decode any consecutive
2d-coordinate window. The intended advantage is polynomial(d,logp)
native character reconstruction in place of exp(O(d logd)) cost. No
hidden root labels or chosen extension-field evaluations are supplied.
Public source roots are the uniformly sampled x inputs, NOT independent
observations of the unknown roots of Q; coupon-collector reasoning does
not supply such observations.

Resource requirements of the proposal are explicit: m fresh copies,
distinctness herald alpha=(p)_m/p^m, and scalar phase chi(a)^d, NOT
chi(a)^m. The resultant sign chi(-1)^(dm) is global. Reversible public
degree-m coefficient conversion, shared-seed root erasure and m+1 field
QFTs cost poly(m,logp,log1/eta) for total approximation error eta; scanning
all windows costs O(m d^3) field operations. Failed heralds consume their
copies. The bound below already concerns the ideal conditional state;
approximation error must be charged, not counted as useful success.
An output-law TV error eta adds at most eta to the success bound; choosing
eta<=d^(-d)/100 uses only O(d logd) additional precision bits.

The corpus been-tried/baselines lookups and a primary-literature check
preceded this calculation. Actual Russell--Shparlinski Section4/Theorem6
provides an O(d)-query POVM under its degree/prime hypothesis, not an
efficient receiver circuit. Actual Ivanyos et al., arXiv:1502.06631,
Theorems8/9 retain e^(d/2) quantum or e^d classical time with classical
power-oracle queries; e=(p-1)/2 is not polynomial in logp. Kopparty,
arXiv:2601.07137, provides the stronger poly(p) FULL-TABLE classical
baseline. Although Theorem1 states d<=epsilon sqrt(p), retain the audited
sufficient Algorithm A/Theorem3.1 condition d<=(epsilon/16)sqrt(p), with
corruption<(1/8-epsilon)p.
Those oracle/table inputs are not supplied by phase copies. Existing
native classical controls and their access distinctions are reused; no
new quantum construction or classical scaling scan is needed for the
algebraic falsifier below. The old uniform exp(O(d logd)) upper bound
remains valid, with no classical hardness or priority claim.

Assume Q is monic irreducible of degree d>=2, p odd, and
2d-1<=m<=p. Let S_m contain all squarefree completely split degree-m
polynomials with nonzero leading scalar. All claims below hold for ANY
normalized state whose coefficient register is supported on S_m,
including arbitrary phases, weights, mixtures and retained workspace.
They therefore already cover more than the clean native source, without
charging any target-dependent state preparation as an available resource.

### Full recurrence event

For H=(ker reduction modQ)^perp, residue fibers have ambient size
K=p^(m+1-d). Put r=m+1-d. Two different R,R' in one fiber cannot share r
rational roots: Q and their root product would both divide R-R', forcing
a nonzero polynomial of degree<=m to have a divisor of degree m+1.
Each R contains binom(m,r) such root subsets, so a fiber contains at most
binom(p,r)/binom(m,r) elements of S_m. Fiberwise Cauchy--Schwarz gives

    Pr(H) <= binom(p,r)/(p^r binom(m,r)) <= (d-1)!/m!.

For arbitrary weights/workspace the same argument applies to the vector
sum in each fiber; scalar phase agreement is not assumed. Conditioning
on distinctness cannot improve the joint probability beyond this bound.
Thus demanding a globally consistent longer trace sequence worsens the
factorial ceiling. This is not yet the bound for discarding coordinates.

### Partial readout and all consecutive windows

For j=0,...,m-2d+1, apply the d-by-d Hankel decoder to
(y_j,...,y_(j+2d-1)). Define the d-dimensional coefficient subspace

    W_j = { X^j Q(X) A(X) : deg A<d }.

Its Fourier annihilator enforces exactly the d Q-recurrences in that
window. The first d window entries determine a unique t in F_p[X]/Q
through the trace pairing. The recurrences force all remaining window
entries to be Tr(t theta^r), r=0,...,2d-1. Irreducibility makes its Hankel
matrix invertible exactly when t!=0. Consequently correct decoding is
W_j^perp with the ZERO WINDOW removed; all outside Fourier coordinates
remain unrestricted. It is not the full-register H minus its origin.

Pulling back the W_j^perp projector averages over affine cosets of W_j,
of size p^d. Coefficients outside this window are fixed within each such
coset. This remains the marginal projector if outside Fourier outcomes
are measured and discarded. Hence success is at most the maximum S_m
occupancy of a coset, divided by p^d.

For j=0, two distinct labels in one coset differ by Q A with deg A<d.
If they shared d rational roots, the same coprimality argument would force
A=0. Counting d-subsets of roots gives

    B_0 <= binom(p,d)/(p^d binom(m,d)) <= (m-d)!/m!.

For j>=1 the difference is X^j Q A. Use d shared NONZERO roots, to avoid
the extra factor X^j. Every R in S_m has at least m-1 nonzero roots, so

    B_j <= binom(p-1,d)/(p^d binom(m-1,d))
        <= (m-d-1)!/(m-1)!.

Neither proof assumes independent windows or independent Fourier outcomes.
A decoder that examines every consecutive window and then verifies any
candidate can succeed only in their union. For m>=2d its probability is
at most

    F_d(m) = (m-d)!/m! + (m-2d+1)(m-d-1)!/(m-1)!.

In fact this is uniformly factorially small for ALL allowed m, not just
m=O(d logd). Set B(m)=(m-d-1)!/(m-1)!. Then

    F_d(m)=B(m)[m-2d+2-d/m],    B(m+1)/B(m)=(m-d)/m.

The difference between successive bracketed expressions, after accounting
for that ratio and multiplying by m, is

    (d-1)(m-2d) + d(m-d)/(m+1) >= 0.

Thus F_d is decreasing for m>=2d. At m=2d it is exactly
(3/2)(d-1)!/(2d-1)!. At m=2d-1 there is only the prefix window and the
previous bound applies. For every allowed packet length,

    Pr(any correct consecutive-window decode)
        <= (3/2)(d-1)!/(2d-1)! <= (3/2)d^(-d).

This is the ideal conditional measurement bound; source failures consume
copies and can only lower joint success. It covers choosing the window
after seeing the entire outcome, but NOT a decoder combining imperfect
windows or multiple failed outcomes to infer Q by another rule. Extra
packet length alone cannot pay growing-degree success for this operation.
No numerical control is necessary: the exact coprimality/packing proof
and elementary monotonicity calculation decide this proposed repair.

Disposition: no packet-length sweep, more-source wrapper or new receiver
subsystem. The constructive question must now change the measurement,
the support, or the way imperfect outcomes are decoded. A paid operation
for that change is still required; these possibilities are UNKNOWN, not
hard or ruled out. In particular do not turn the source labels into
unavailable hidden-root observations. This scoped rejection leaves the
known parameterized receiver and all previous exact controls intact.

# Native character Fourier features and the exact mask marginal

2026-11-06. Parent derivations, independent Codex actual-text review and
Claude targeted proof audit complete; review dispositions below. No new
end-to-end decoder is claimed.

## Scientific contract and choice

Input is an odd prime p, degree d and unknown monic squarefree Q over F_p.
The native copy source is p^(-1/2) sum_x F(x)|x>, with F a fixed sign table;
clean F(x)=lambda(Q(x)), lambda(0)=+1. The stronger chosen-BIT model supplies
F(x) on chosen classical inputs as well as coherent queries. These access
models are NOT interchangeable. The target is Q in poly(d,logp) time.

The existing uniform algorithm costs exp(O(d logd))*poly(logp), and its exact
consecutive-window Hankel readout has success<=1.5d^-d for irreducible Q
and every packet size 2d-1<=m<=p.
The candidate tested here was a decoder extracting imperfect-output Fourier
features or treating output labels as ideal moments plus independent public
mask noise. This might avoid waiting for a fully correct recurrence packet.
No new quantum subsystem is needed to test these hypotheses.

Prior work: corpus been-tried and baselines lookups (2026-11-06) supplied no
exact catalog match. Actual Russell--Shparlinski0212016 Theorem6 is an
O(d)-QUERY/POVM result, not an efficient decoder. Kopparty2601.07137 actual
Introduction and AlgorithmA/Theorem3.1 give a full-field-table classical
algorithm with polynomial field-size cost, under their degree/error bounds.
These are upper bounds, not hardness. The fixed-degree chosen-line
multivariate composition inherits the univariate cost. Independent new
superlattice DGS still uses exponential lists and has no paid clean inverse;
see SUPERLATTICE_CONDITIONAL_RECORD_AUDIT.md. These comparisons motivated
one focused test of a genuinely different decoder interface here.

## 1. Every additive Fourier mean has a matched classical estimator

Let m>=1, p>=m, V=F_p^(m+1), D=|V| and S the set of all degree-m squarefree
completely split polynomials with nonzero leading coefficient. Let
N=|S|=(p-1)binom(p,m). The paid source of the Hankel note is

 |S_F> = N^(-1/2) sum_{R in S} s_F(R)|R>,
 s_F(R)=chi(lead R)^d product_{x: R(x)=0} F(x).

Here d is the TARGET degree even if m differs. Coefficients are ascending.
Let P_F(y) be its normalized additive Fourier measurement law. Expanding
squared amplitudes and using character orthogonality proves, for every
public coefficient shift h in V,

 E_{y~P_F} exp(2*pi*i*<h,y>/p)
   = (1/N) sum_{R in S, R+h in S} s_F(R)s_F(R+h).             (1)

The source is real, so its Fourier law is even and the mean is real; a
choice of Fourier sign replaces h by-h without changing (1).

Classical algorithm in the chosen-BIT model: sample R uniformly in S by a
uniform leading coefficient and uniform m-subset of F_p. Form and factor
PUBLIC R+h. Return0 unless it has exact degree m, nonzero leading
coefficient and m distinct linear factors. Otherwise query the two root
sets (at most2m native signs), and return s_F(R)s_F(R+h). This bounded
random variable is an unbiased estimator of (1). Sampling a uniform subset,
public finite-field polynomial factorization and all field operations cost
randomized poly(m,logp). No split-event postselection is performed: failures
are zero observations, not expensive rejected samples. Q is never read.
Uniform subset sampling can use sequential sampling without replacement
with a finite-index map; it does not require a p-sized table.

For a fixed public upper bound K on adaptively chosen shifts and additive
accuracy epsilon, use
O(epsilon^-2 log(K/delta)) independent observations per query, with standard
bounded clocks for finite-field factoring and random-bit generation and
failure allocated within delta. A timed-out routine ABORTS the whole run;
it must not report a zero observation. Use Floyd's m-draw subset algorithm
and capped exact uniform draws. Split/squarefree membership itself is
deterministic by checking R+h divides X^p-X; only root extraction needs
randomized factorization. The conditional Hoeffding guarantee holds
for each query given the preceding transcript; union bound gives simultaneous
accuracy. Cost is poly(K,m,logp,epsilon^-1,log1/delta), including native sign
queries. The exact law holds for ANY fixed F, including a fixed corrupted
character table. It does not cover arbitrary amplitude-weighted sources.

Consequently a decoder whose guarantee holds for ANY epsilon-accurate
statistical-query answers to polynomially many additive Fourier means is
classically matched at inverse-polynomial epsilon in the chosen-BIT model.
Matching means alone does not reproduce finite-estimator randomness, joint
adaptive sample laws, or an algorithm exploiting those laws. It does not
sample P_F, simulate arbitrary functions of Fourier labels, recover Q, or
apply to a copy-only source. A successful decoder using this interface would
be a classical algorithm too, not an oracle separation in the chosen-BIT model.

This also covers the complete-syndrome score of any PUBLIC candidate: for
any supplied subspace B<=V and coset representative z, the projector identity
is 1_{y in z+B^perp}=E_{h uniform B} exp(2*pi*i*<h,y-z>/p).
Sample h from B and return cos(2*pi*<h,z>/p) times the estimator above.
Its expectation is P_F(z+B^perp), its magnitude is at most1, and its additive-
epsilon cost remains polynomial in the input basis size,m,logp,epsilon^-1.
Evaluate cosine to error<=epsilon/2 with polynomially many precision bits.
This scores a candidate to additive accuracy; it neither finds the unknown
candidate nor supplies relative accuracy for exponentially small scores.

## 2. Syndrome marginal is mask-only; the full law is not independent noise

Now restrict to CLEAN monic irreducible Q, degree d>=2, m>=d. Let
L:V->A=F_p[X]/Q, W=ker L, K0=|W|=p^(m+1-d), H=W^perp. On every residue
fiber S_v={R in S:R modQ=v}, s_F(R) is, up to one global sign, chi_A(v).
No split R is divisible by Q, so v!=0 on S.

Let |M>=N^(-1/2) sum_{R in S}|R> be the PUBLIC unsigned split mask, with
Fourier law P_M. For EVERY coset z+H, the Fourier projector gives

 P_F(z+H) = 1/(N*K0) sum_v
        |sum_{R in S_v} exp(2*pi*i*<z,R>/p)|^2
          = P_M(z+H).                                      (2)

The character phase cancels inside each fiber. Thus the complete syndrome
(y modulo H, equivalently all true-Q recurrences) has EXACTLY the public
mask's induced marginal. This is not just equality of the zero syndrome.
Computing that syndrome requires Q, so (2) supplies no native decoder or
simulator. The same fiber-phase proof in fact works for any root-free Q,
even reducible or non-squarefree, since the determinant of multiplication
by R in F_p[X]/Q still equals the resultant and never vanishes here.
The ideal uniform H\{0} law below, however, requires irreducibility.
For Q with rational roots, zero padding breaks this norm-phase argument;
(2) is not asserted in that case or for corrupted F.

A tempting stronger model takes independent T uniform on H\{0} (the ideal
irreducible norm-character Fourier law) and Z~P_M, then asserts y=T+Z.
It too has (2), but its FULL LABEL law is generally wrong: Fourier amplitudes
convolve coherently, and taking squares retains cross terms.

Cheapest exact counterexample REUSES the existing p5 irreducible control:
Q=X^2+2,d2,m3,N40,K0=25,D625. Existing exact residue counts give energy
sum_v |S_v|^2=72 and signed sum8. Therefore

 P_F(0)=8/3125,
 P_M(H)=9/125, P_M(0)=8/125,
 Pr[T+Z=0]=(P_M(H)-P_M(0))/(|H|-1)=1/3000.

These are unequal. Both models nevertheless have the SAME complete
true-Q syndrome law. A check of total mass on H or even every syndrome
would miss this error. This refutes this independent full-label noise
model, not all imperfect-outcome decoders. The zero label is singular for
Hankel decoding, but is a legitimate receiver outcome. Artifacts reused:
classical_baselines/hankel_resultant_control.json and the exact counting
calculation recorded in LEGENDRE_HANKEL_SUCCESS_BOUNDARY.md. No new FFT,
parameter sweep or quantum routine is needed for this falsifier.

The exact identity also fails throughout the large-prime regime for EVERY
odd d>=3, irreducible Q and nonempty split source m>=d. Scaling the leading
coefficient multiplies the actual source sign by chi(a)^d, so P_F(0)=0.
Write U=p^d-1 and C_v=|S_v|. C_0=0 and Cauchy--Schwarz give
sum C_v^2>=N^2/U. The proposed mixture instead has

 Pr[T+Z=0]=[sum C_v^2/(N*K0)-N/D]/U >= N/(D*U^2)>0,

using D=K0*p^d. This is an exact-identity counterexample under theorem-sized
primes too. The difference can be tiny: no useful total-variation lower
bound or rejection of a CONTROLLED APPROXIMATION follows from it.

## 3. Recurrence rows are not mostly correct

For m>=d, let s_i(y)=<X^i Q,y>, 0<=i<=m-d. The event s_i=0 is a Fourier
projector averaging over affine cosets of span(X^iQ), each of size p.
For i=0, two distinct split labels in one such coset share no root:
a shared root would be a root of cQ, impossible for root-free Q.
Thus each coset contains at most floor(p/m) split labels. For i>0, distinct
labels share no NONZERO root, and each has at least m-1 nonzero roots;
occupancy is at most floor((p-1)/(m-1)). Fiberwise Cauchy--Schwarz yields

 Pr(s_0=0)<=floor(p/m)/p<=1/m,
 Pr(s_i=0)<=floor((p-1)/(m-1))/p<1/(m-1), i>0.

This holds even for arbitrary weights and retained ancillary vectors on
